sections.h2: Which parts of Erie County does the Town of Amherst cover?
sections.html:
Amherst sits in the northern part of Erie County and is Buffalo's largest suburb by population. Its 53.6 square miles (53.2 of them land) held an estimated 130,442 people in mid-2025. Tonawanda Creek forms the northern boundary with Niagara County, and Ellicott Creek crosses the town.

Most of the names on an Amherst address are hamlets or post-office areas with no government of their own. Williamsville is the exception, an incorporated village inside the town.

  • Eggertsville and Snyder, in the older southwest, near Buffalo
  • Williamsville, the incorporated village in the south
  • Getzville and the Audubon area, near the center
  • East Amherst and Swormville, shared with the Town of Clarence
  • North Bailey, around Bailey Avenue and Maple Road

Mailing addresses can cross town lines. Some homes east of Transit Road carry a Williamsville address yet belong to the Town of Clarence for taxes and schools, so read the tax bill to see which municipality applies.

sections.h2: What turned Amherst from farmland into a suburb?
sections.html:
The state carved Amherst out of the Town of Buffalo on April 10, 1818. After the Erie Canal opened in 1825, German farmers took up the northern land and mills went up along Ellicott Creek. Williamsville began in the 1810s, Eggertsville and Snyder in the 1830s, East Amherst and Swormville in the 1850s and Getzville in the 1860s.

The real surge came after World War II. Census counts read 13,181 in 1930, 31,407 in 1950, 90,734 in 1970 and 129,595 in 2020. Nearly tripling in twenty years suggests many of today's subdivisions date to that stretch.

A house that age may need work on kitchens, baths and mechanical systems. A financed buyer may negotiate repairs, and a cash buyer will usually fold them into the price.

sections.h2: How do Amherst's housing numbers compare with the rest of New York?
sections.html:
Owners live in 69.9% of Amherst homes, and the Census Bureau puts a typical owned home at $311,600.

Over one resident in five is 65 or older, and 86.4% were at the same address a year earlier. Long tenure like that often ends in a downsize or an estate sale.

sections.h2: Which school district is a house in, and what colleges are nearby?
sections.html:
Four public districts divide the town. Williamsville Central is the biggest, taking the eastern half and some of Clarence. Amherst Central has the southwest, around Eggertsville and Snyder, with Amherst Central High School. Sweet Home Central has the northwest, including West Amherst and Getzville, and Clarence Central has a small southeastern corner.

Colleges add renters and buyers. The University at Buffalo's North Campus lies here, along with Daemen University, an Erie Community College campus and a Bryant and Stratton College campus.

Name the district whenever you describe the house. Two homes sharing a ZIP code can fall in different districts.

sections.h2: What roads and weather should an Amherst seller keep in mind?
sections.html:
The Thruway (I-90) crosses the south end. I-290 cuts diagonally toward Tonawanda, and I-990, the Lockport Expressway, lies wholly inside Amherst and ends at Millersport Highway.

Surface routes tie the hamlets together. US 62 marks the west line as Niagara Falls Boulevard, then carries on as Sheridan Drive and Bailey Avenue. Main Street is Route 5, Transit Road (Route 78) is the east line, and Harlem Road, Campbell Boulevard and Sheridan Drive are Routes 240, 270 and 324.

Average highs span 31 to 47 degrees from November to March and 60 to 81 from May to October, so a long cold season makes roof, gutter and furnace condition easy to notice during a showing.

sections.h2: What do Amherst's rental rules mean if tenants live in the house?
sections.html:
Chapter 44 of the town code bars renting a unit until the owner holds a rental registration certificate. An owner-occupied property with two or fewer units, if not used for short stays, is exempt.

  • The standard certificate lasts up to three years, with a $75 inspection fee for each unit.
  • Stays of 1 to 30 days count as short-term rentals. Those certificates last one year, come with an annual inspection, and cost $250 a unit if the owner lives there or $500 if not, per the 2025 form.
  • No certificate issues until the unit passes inspection and local property taxes are current.
  • Owners living outside Erie, Niagara and Genesee counties need a local agent.
  • Houses built before 1978 carry a lead paint certification on the form.

A buyer can take over a certificate's remaining term by filing a transfer application with the Commissioner of Building within 30 days of the deed. Skipping registration can double the fee, add a $75 fine and lead to a notice to vacate, and a code violation can bring up to $1,500 or 15 days in jail.

sections.h2: How do assessment complaints and county tax liens work in Amherst?
sections.html:
The town Assessor values each parcel, and an owner who disagrees files RP-524. Most communities use the fourth Tuesday in May as the cutoff, which would be May 25 in 2027, so confirm it with the Assessor's Office at 5583 Main Street in Williamsville. That office has taken paperwork by mail or drop-off as well as hearings in person.

Erie County may foreclose liens that sit unpaid for two years or longer. The In Rem 173 action started September 9, 2025 for 2022 and earlier liens, with November 10, 2025 as the final redemption date. To redeem, an owner paid the back taxes and a $500 statutory fee by cash, certified check, bank check or money order to the County Director of Real Property Tax Services. Parcels not redeemed head to public auction, and later years' taxes continue to accrue.

If back taxes are owed, request a payoff figure from Erie County Real Property Tax Services, since the balance grows with fees and interest. Closing proceeds can retire a lien, so have the title company order the figure early.

sections.h2: What will the state tax cost on an Amherst sale, and which sale routes exist?
sections.html:
The state taxes a conveyance at two dollars per $500 of price, a cost that usually falls on the seller. The Erie County Clerk takes the TP-584 return, due 15 days after the deed changes hands.

Owners can hire an agent, sell without one or accept a cash offer. An agent sale involves showings and a closing date set by the buyer's lender. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition, which suits a rental near the end of its certificate, an inherited house or a parcel with back taxes.

Whichever you pick, locate the deed, the latest town and school tax bills, any rental certificate and your lender's payoff statement.

faqs.q: Does a tenant-occupied Amherst house need a rental certificate at sale?
faqs.a: Registration is the owner's duty while the unit is rented. A buyer can take it over by filing within 30 days of the deed, so hand over the certificate and inspection paperwork.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for contesting an Amherst assessment?
faqs.a: Most New York communities use the fourth Tuesday in May. Check the exact day with the Amherst Assessor's Office. The form is RP-524, and there is no charge to file.

faqs.q: What happens when county tax liens stay unpaid on an Amherst property?
faqs.a: Erie County can foreclose once liens are two or more years old. Owners receive notice and a last redemption date, with a $500 fee, and anything left unredeemed goes to public auction.

faqs.q: What would the state transfer tax be on a typical Amherst sale?
faqs.a: At two dollars per $500, a sale at the Census value of $311,600 owes about $1,248, since each partial $500 counts as a full one.

faqs.q: How do I find which district my Amherst house belongs to?
faqs.a: It is one of Williamsville, Amherst, Sweet Home or Clarence Central, depending on location. The tax bill names it, and the Assessor's Office can confirm.
